title: 5 Tips for Safer Intercity Travel in Nigeria (2026)
excerpt: Night travel can be risky. Learn how to choose safe companies like GIGM and GUO, pick the safest seats, and avoid common road hazards.
content:
Traveling by road in Nigeria requires smart planning. While new highways are being built, safety remains the #1 concern for travelers from Lagos to Abuja, Port Harcourt, and beyond. Here are the 5 non-negotiable rules for safe travel in 2026.

1. Choose Companies with Vehicle Tracking

Not all 'transport companies' are the same. We strongly recommend booking with established operators like GIGM (God is Good Motors) or GUO Transport. Why? Because they use real-time vehicle tracking. If a bus breaks down or goes off-route, their HQ knows immediately.

2. The '6 AM Rule' (Avoid Night Travel)

While night buses are often cheaper, they are significantly riskier due to poor visibility and security issues on highways like the Ore-Benin express. Always book the first bus (6:00 AM - 7:00 AM). You can check morning departure prices here.

3. Seat Selection Matters

Did you know the safest seat in a Toyota Hiace is usually in the middle row, aisle side? Avoid the seat directly next to the driver (the 'death seat') and the very back row, which feels the most impact from potholes.

4. Share Your Live Location

Before you leave the terminal, send your Manifest ID (printed on your ticket) and your live WhatsApp location to a family member. Established parks take passenger manifests seriously—roadside buses do not.

5. Carry Cash (But Not Too Much)

ATM networks can be unreliable at rest stops in Lokoja or Ore. Keep N5,000 - N10,000 in smaller notes for food, but keep your main funds on your card.

title: Lagos to Abuja Price Guide (2026): Who is Cheapest?
excerpt: A complete price breakdown for Lagos to Abuja by bus. We compare GIGM, ABC, and GUO prices for Sienna, Coaster, and Luxury buses.
content:
The Lagos to Abuja route is the busiest travel corridor in Nigeria. Whether you are traveling for business or Japa plans, prices fluctuate wildly depending on the vehicle type (Sienna vs. Coaster) and the terminal location (Jibowu vs. Iyana Ipaja).

Current Price Ranges (2026 Estimates)

  • Luxury Bus (Marcopolo): NGN 35,000 - N45,000
  • Toyota Sienna (AC): NGN 45,000 - N55,000
  • Coaster/Hummer Bus: NGN 25,000 - N32,000

Note: Prices change daily based on fuel costs. Use our Search Tool for today's live rates.

1. GIGM (God is Good Motors)

GIGM is the premium choice. Their 'Prime' terminals in Jibowu and Ikeja offer air-conditioned waiting rooms. Expect to pay a premium, but their fleet is the newest on the road. Safety rating: 9/10.

2. GUO Transport

GUO is the king of the East, but their Lagos-Abuja route is excellent. They are often N2,000 - N3,000 cheaper than GIGM and allow more luggage allowance. Great for traders.

3. ABC Transport

If comfort is your priority, ABC's 'Sleeper' buses are legendary. They take longer because they adhere to strict speed limits (which is a good thing for safety). Read our Guide on Travel Safety to see why speed limits matter.

Verdict: Who should you choose?

If you have a tight budget, look for Young Shall Grow or smaller operators at Jibowu. If you prioritize speed and AC, stick to GIGM Sienna.

title: Iyare Motors Price List 2026: The "Benin King" of Road Travel?
excerpt: Traveling from Benin to Lagos? Iyare Motors is the crowd favorite. We review their 2026 price list, terminal locations in Jibowu and Utako, and why they might be better than GIGM.
content:
If you have ever traveled from Edo State to Lagos, you know the name Iyare Motors. In the Benin dialect, "Iyare" means "Safe Journey," and for decades, this company has been the backbone of transport in the South-South region.

But in 2026, with fuel prices rising and competition from tech-focused companies like GIGM, is Iyare still the king of the road? Let's break down their prices, terminals, and service quality.

Iyare Motors Price List (2026 Estimates)

Iyare is famous for finding the "sweet spot" between luxury and affordability. They are generally cheaper than GIGM but more reliable than roadside buses.

  • Benin to Lagos (Sienna) ₦18,000 - ₦22,000
  • Lagos to Benin ₦18,000 - ₦22,000
  • Benin to Abuja ₦28,000 - ₦32,000
  • Lagos to Abuja ₦30,000 - ₦35,000

Note: Prices change during festive periods. Check the Official Iyare Motors Page for today's updates.

The Terminals: Where to Board

Iyare operates strictly from their own terminals, which adds a layer of security. Their most popular hubs include:

  • Benin City (The HQ): The Urubi Terminal in Benin is massive. It is the heart of their operations and usually has the most frequent departures.
  • Lagos (Maza-Maza & Jibowu): If you are on the mainland, their Jibowu park is efficient. For those near Festac, the Maza-Maza terminal helps you avoid Third Mainland Bridge traffic.
  • Abuja (Utako): Located in the transport hub of Utako, right next to competitors like ABC.

The Verdict: Should You Book?

Pros:

  • Drivers are extremely experienced on the Ore-Benin road.
  • Prices are consistently fair.
  • Good AC in their Sienna fleet.

Cons:

  • Online booking isn't as smooth as GIGM.
  • Terminals can get rowdy during holidays.

Final Word: If you are traveling to or from Edo State, Iyare is unbeatable. For purely Lagos-Abuja trips, you might find more luxury elsewhere, but Iyare gets the job done safely.

title: ABC Transport Price List 2026: Sleeper Coach Fares Explained
excerpt: ABC Transport's Sleeper Coach is a favorite for long routes. We break down 2026 prices, comfort levels, and whether the extra cost is worth it.
content:
ABC Transport has been on Nigerian roads for decades, and its 'Sleeper Coach' service remains one of the most talked-about options for long-distance travel. Here's what it actually costs in 2026.

Standard vs. Sleeper Coach

ABC runs two main tiers:

  • Standard Coach: A regular AC bus, priced similarly to GUO and Peace Mass Transit.
  • Sleeper Coach: Reclining, bed-style seats designed for overnight or very long routes. Expect a premium of 20-30% over standard fares.

Is the Sleeper Coach Worth It?

For routes over 8 hours, like Lagos to Kano or Lagos to Maiduguri, the Sleeper Coach can be a genuine upgrade in comfort. For shorter hops like Lagos to Ibadan, it's rarely worth the extra cost.

Terminal Locations

ABC operates from major parks including Jibowu and Ojota in Lagos, and Utako in Abuja. Because they adhere to strict speed limits, journeys can take slightly longer than competitors — a trade-off many travelers are happy to make for safety, as covered in our safety guide.

title: Solo Female Travel in Nigeria: Safety Tips and Ticket Price Guide
excerpt: Traveling solo as a woman comes with extra considerations. Here's how to pick the right company, seat, and price without compromising on safety.
content:
Traveling solo as a woman often comes with additional considerations, and Nigeria is no exception. The good news: with the right preparation, intercity travel by road can be safe, affordable, and stress-free.

Choose Companies with Manifest Systems

Stick to established operators like GIGM or Peace Mass Transit, which record every passenger's details on a manifest. This adds a layer of accountability that roadside buses don't offer.

Seat and Timing Tips

Book a window seat closer to the middle of the bus, and avoid the last bus of the day where possible. Morning departures, covered in our full safety guide, are generally the safest option.

Price Doesn't Have to Mean Compromise

You don't need to pay for the most expensive ticket to travel safely — mid-range operators like GUO and ABC Transport have solid safety records too. Use our Budget Planner to find safe, affordable options within your price range.

title: Ember Months Travel: Why Bus Fares Spike (And How to Save)
excerpt: Fares can jump 40-60% during the ember months. Here's why it happens every year and practical ways to avoid paying the surge price.
content:
Every year, from September through December, intercity transport fares in Nigeria climb steadily. Travelers call it the 'ember months surge,' and it catches many people off guard. Here's what's really going on, and how to save.

Why Fares Increase

  • Demand spikes: More people travel home for the holidays, especially in December.
  • Return-leg pricing: Buses that arrive full but leave empty raise prices to cover the empty return trip.
  • Fuel cost timing: Fuel prices often rise toward year-end, adding pressure to fares.

How to Save During This Period

  1. Travel mid-week instead of Fridays or the last weekend before Christmas.
  2. Book earlier in the day — last-minute evening tickets are usually the most expensive.
  3. Compare multiple operators instead of defaulting to your usual choice, since price gaps widen during peak season.

title: Hiring a Private Driver in Nigeria: What It Really Costs in 2026
excerpt: Not every trip needs a bus ticket. Here's what hiring a private driver or chartering a car for intercity travel typically costs, and when it's worth it.
content:
In Nigeria's bustling cities and beyond, hiring a private driver or chartering a vehicle has become an increasingly popular alternative to standard bus travel — especially for families, small groups, or anyone carrying a lot of luggage.

What Affects the Price

  • Distance: Longer routes naturally cost more, both in fuel and driver time.
  • Vehicle type: A standard sedan is cheaper than an SUV or a Sienna-style minivan.
  • Round trip vs. one-way: Drivers often charge more for a one-way trip since they have to return empty.

Charter vs. Standard Bus Ticket

For a solo traveler, a scheduled bus ticket is almost always cheaper. But for a family of four or five, splitting the cost of a private charter can work out close to — or even cheaper than — buying that many individual tickets, while also saving time by skipping terminal waits.

How to Decide

Compare the total charter quote against what a full set of tickets would cost on a standard route using our price search tool. If you're traveling with kids, elderly relatives, or a lot of cargo, the convenience of a private driver is often worth the premium.
